title: Finite-projective inverse formula for a normalized scalar sheaf-dual comparison
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $(\mathcal C,J)$ a site small in the chosen module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $B$ be a sheaf of commutative rings with a morphism $\alpha:\underline R\to B$, where underlines denote constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For an $R$-module $V$, let $\underline V$ be its constant module sheaf [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] and put $C_B(V)=B\otimes_{\underline R}\underline V$, using module sheaves and ordinary sheaf tensor [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $V^*=\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,R)$ and use internal sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. In formulas with $r\in R$ in a section of $B$, $r$ means the image under $\alpha$ of the constant section $r$.
Assume $V$ is finitely generated and projective [def-weil-finitely-generated-module, def-weil-pbc-projective-module], and let $\beta:C_B(V^*)\to\mathcal Hom_B(C_B(V),B)$ be any $B$-linear sheaf morphism satisfying $\beta(b\otimes\phi)(b'\otimes v)=bb'\alpha(\phi(v))$ on all localized sites. There exist $N\geq0$ and linear maps $i:V\to R^N$, $p:R^N\to V$ with $pi=1_V$. For every such splitting put $v_j=p(e_j)$ and $\lambda_j=e_j^*i$, using the standard basis and coordinates of $R^N$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. They satisfy
$$v=\sum_j\lambda_j(v)v_j,\qquad \phi=\sum_j\phi(v_j)\lambda_j.$$
For every object $U$ and section $h\in\mathcal Hom_B(C_B(V),B)(U)$, equivalently a morphism $C_B(V)|_U\to B|_U$ on the localized ringed site [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], set
$$\gamma_U(h)=\sum_j h(1\otimes v_j)\otimes\lambda_j\in C_B(V^*)(U).$$
The maps $\gamma_U$ are $B(U)$-linear and commute with restriction, hence define a sheaf morphism $\gamma$. They satisfy $\beta\gamma=1$ and $\gamma\beta=1$, including on sections not globally expressible as pure tensors. Thus $\beta$ is an isomorphism with inverse $\gamma$, and $\gamma$ is independent of the chosen splitting. The assertion includes $N=0$, $V=0$ and non-flat $B$ over $\underline R$.

proof.text: Choose generators $w_1,\ldots,w_N$ of $V$ and define the surjection $p:R^N\to V$ by $p(e_j)=w_j$. The lifting characterization of projectivity applied to $1_V:V\to V$ and this surjection supplies $i:V\to R^N$ with $pi=1_V$. This proves existence; henceforth take ANY splitting as in the statement. For $V=0$ the empty generating family gives $N=0$.

source.place: Tags 05CE and 05CF, definition-projective and lemma-characterize-projective, proof of projective implies a summand: choose a surjection from a free module and split it.

proof.text: Expand $i(v)=\sum_j\lambda_j(v)e_j$ in the standard coordinates and apply $p$. This gives $v=\sum_j\lambda_j(v)v_j$. Applying any $\phi:V\to R$ to this identity gives, as an equality of functionals, $\phi=\sum_j\phi(v_j)\lambda_j$. In particular the maps $t:V^*\to R^N$, $t(\phi)=(\phi(v_j))_j$, and $q:R^N\to V^*$, $q((a_j))=\sum_j a_j\lambda_j$, satisfy $qt=1_{V^*}$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, final finite-free/direct-summand calculation, expanded for constant-module scalar extension; sites-modules.tex Section 03EK and Section 04TT.

proof.text: Write $E=C_B(V)$ and $D=C_B(V^*)$. Constant-module sheafification and tensoring act on a linear map $f$ by the map induced from $b\otimes v\mapsto b\otimes f(v)$; this preserves identities and composition by the uniqueness in sheafification. Apply $C_B$ to $pi=1$ and $qt=1$. The finite-power isomorphism $C_B(R^N)\cong B^N$ of the cited presentation-extension node sends $b\otimes(a_j)$ to $(b\alpha(a_j))_j$ and its inverse sends $(b_j)$ to $\sum_j b_j\otimes e_j$. Thus for EVERY object $T$ and EVERY $x\in E(T)$, taking the coordinates $(a_j)$ of $C_B(i)(x)$ gives $x=\sum_j a_j(1\otimes v_j)$. Likewise EVERY $y\in D(T)$ has an expansion $y=\sum_j c_j(1\otimes\lambda_j)$, by taking the coordinates of $C_B(t)(y)$ and applying $C_B(q)$. The formulas for $C_B(p)$ and $C_B(q)$ follow on each basis vector and then by $B(T)$-linearity on $B(T)^N$. These are global finite expansions from a split retraction, not an assertion that arbitrary sections of a sheaf tensor are pure tensors. No exactness or flatness is used.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, final finite-free/direct-summand calculation, expanded for constant-module scalar extension; sites-modules.tex Section 03EK and Section 04TT.

proof.text: For $h\in\mathcal Hom_B(E,B)(U)$ define $\gamma_U(h)=\sum_j h_U(1\otimes v_j)\otimes\lambda_j$. Evaluation and the sum are additive, and $\gamma_U(a h)=a\gamma_U(h)$ for $a\in B(U)$. For $f:T\to U$, naturality of the localized morphism $h$ gives $B(f)(h_U(1\otimes v_j))=(h|_T)_T(1\otimes v_j)$. Restrictions of the constant generators $v_j,\lambda_j$ are the same generators. Restricting the finite sum therefore gives exactly $\gamma_T(h|_T)$, so these maps form a $B$-linear sheaf morphism.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, final finite-free/direct-summand calculation, expanded for constant-module scalar extension; sites-modules.tex Section 03EK and Section 04TT.

proof.text: For $T\to U$ and $v\in V$, normalization and the first dual-generator identity give $(\beta_U\gamma_U(h))_T(1\otimes v)=\sum_j h_T(1\otimes v_j)\alpha(\lambda_j(v))=h_T(1\otimes v)$. Both localized maps are $B$-linear. The expansion of every $x\in E(T)$ from step 3, valid for every $T\to U$, extends this equality to all sections. Thus they are equal as morphisms on $\mathcal C/U$, which means $\beta\gamma=1$.

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, final finite-free/direct-summand calculation, expanded for constant-module scalar extension; sites-modules.tex Section 03EK and Section 04TT.

proof.text: For $b\in B(U)$ and $\phi\in V^*$, normalization gives $\gamma_U\beta_U(b\otimes\phi)=\sum_j b\alpha(\phi(v_j))\otimes\lambda_j=b\otimes\sum_j\phi(v_j)\lambda_j=b\otimes\phi$. The second expansion in step 3 and $B(U)$-linearity extend this equality to every $y\in D(U)$, proving $\gamma\beta=1$. If $\gamma\prime$ comes from any other splitting, $\gamma\prime=\gamma\prime\beta\gamma=\gamma$, so the inverse is independent of it. When $N=0$, the split retractions in step 3 give $E=D=0$, and all sums and identities still hold. The same argument covers $V=0$ with a nonzero chosen $N$, the zero ring, the zero coefficient sheaf and non-flat $B$.
